en.title: El Salvador's Bukele expected to seek third term as leader
en.dek: Bukele to register candidacy for third term ahead of February elections
en.context: Bukele came to power in 2019, ending three decades of rule by the ARENA and FMLN parties. The Supreme Court later ruled that sitting presidents could seek reelection, and his 2024 election victory led to a 2025 constitutional amendment allowing indefinite reelections.

problemsFixed: Facts in body not supported by sources (e.g. 'Bukele would face four opposition candidates' — source lists 2 named candidates; '55% to 70% support' — source says 'polls' but does not give exact range in the excerpt; 'Supreme Court ruled in 2024' — source says 2025 amendment; '2024 election victory' — source says 2024 vote but amendment was 2025)
Loaded language: 'consolidate power indefinitely without institutional checks and balances' is a claim from rights groups, not a neutral fact; 'harmed due process and innocent lives' is evaluative
Context paragraph contains evaluative framing ('ending three decades of rule')
Repetition: 'Bukele' opens multiple sentences; summary sentence at end evaluates outcome
